name: Oriol.Design
tagline: One-page portfolio of Oriol Bedia, a design leader in Barcelona who led teams at Typeform, Zalando and Bitpanda
description:
Oriol.Design is the personal site of Oriol Bedia, a product design leader in Barcelona. The page says he has 15+ years in design and 5+ years in leadership and design ops. It names Typeform, Zalando and Bitpanda as employers, and Design Manager at Bitpanda as his most recent role.

The page offers three roles: Design Leader, Design Manager and Design Mentor. Each role has five core skills and a booking link. The mentor block gives a 4.8 rating and 100+ sessions. Short case blocks follow, for example a Typeform design and research team that grew from 5 to 15 people.

The site is built in Framer. The page says he is open to work, full-time, on a permanent or freelance basis.
pricing_detail: The page shows no prices. Contact is by email (hola@oriol.design) or a booking link.
agent_guidance:
Fetch the home page. Framer renders the text into the HTML, so a plain fetch returns the bio, the three role blocks and the case summaries. Each block appears three or four times, one copy for each breakpoint. Remove the copies before you quote the text.

The sitemap lists only the home page and /404. The site has no case-study pages and no llms.txt.
why_it_matters: It shows how a design manager presents leadership work: team size, process and outcomes, with few screens.
tier_reason: The bio, the employers and the team-growth numbers are in the HTML. Held at C because the work is short text blocks with no case-study pages, and the sitemap lists only the home page.
notable_for: design leadership at Typeform, Zalando and Bitpanda

The page reads "Over the past years, I led teams across B2B SaaS, B2C e-commerce, fintech, and Web3 at Typeform, Zalando, and Bitpanda.", "Most recently, Design Manager at Bitpanda." and "I helped scale a design & research team from 5 to 15 by setting-up its culture and processes". /sitemap.xml 200 lists / and /404. /llms.txt 404.

name: Ugur Turgut
tagline: Brand, product and web designer in New York whose project work sits behind a password
description:
Ugur Turgut is a designer who works on brand strategy, visual identity, product design and websites. The page shows a New York clock in Eastern Time. It lists nine services, from Brand Strategy to No-code Development.

Most of the public text is an essay about brands whose look, message and product do not connect. The project work is not public. A "Private work" panel asks for a password, and visitors without one must ask for access.

The site is hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript (css/site.css and js/main.js), with no framework markers. Contact is through X, LinkedIn, email and a Cal.com link.
pricing_detail: The page shows no prices. Contact is by email or a Cal.com booking link.
agent_guidance:
Fetch the home page for the services list and the essay text. Do not expect case studies. The work is behind a password, so an agent cannot read it.

/llms.txt and /sitemap.xml both return HTTP 200, but they serve the home page HTML. Treat both files as absent.
why_it_matters: It is a designer site that sells with written positioning and keeps the portfolio private.
tier_reason: The services list and the positioning essay are in the HTML. Held at C because the project work needs a password, so no case study can be checked.

name: Kuba Gawlik
tagline: Portfolio of a designer in Cracow who makes brands and Framer websites for tech and AI companies
description:
heykuba.com is the portfolio of Kuba Gawlik, a designer in Cracow, Poland. He makes brands and websites, mostly for tech and AI companies. The page lists ten client projects, among them BTQ, PayPath, Bynario, Concourse, The Signal, PAX and Cluster. Each project has a short summary and a scope tag such as "web + brand + 3d". All but one link to the live site.

An FAQ explains the process. He builds only in Framer, with the developer Kamil Leśniak. Most projects take 4 to 8 weeks, and communication runs on Slack or Telegram.

The page lists features and awards, for example an Awwwards Honourable Mention and seven Land-book features. The site is built in Framer.
pricing_detail: The page shows no prices. A form requests a quote, and the FAQ says scope, timeline and budget are agreed on a short call.
agent_guidance:
Fetch the home page. The project summaries, the FAQ and the about text are in the HTML. The project list appears more than once, one copy for each breakpoint.

Follow the LIVE SITE links to see the shipped work. The sitemap lists only the home page, and the site has no llms.txt.
why_it_matters: It is a solo designer site that names real clients, links to each live site and states the process and project length.
tier_reason: Ten named client projects, nine with live-site links, and the FAQ gives the build tool, the team and a 4 to 8 week timeline. Held at B because each project is a short summary on one page, with no case-study pages, and the sitemap lists only the home page.
notable_for: Framer-only builds with a partner developer
brands and websites for tech and AI companies

name: Marius Bălaj
tagline: Personal site of an engineer turned founder, with writing, a bookshelf and a training log
description:
Marius Bălaj is a software engineer and founder in Romania. In 2021 he co-founded QED, which Sandbox acquired. He is now Managing Director (Romania) at Sandbox. Before that he was a senior engineer at stake.fish / f2pool.io and a lead engineer at Alacritylaw.

The home page is a short column of text. It holds the bio, an experience list with dates, recent writing, a bookshelf and his latest training sessions. He is also president of Viitorul Boxing Club.

The site runs on Next.js. It publishes an llms.txt and a sitemap. The llms.txt names an article about the Sandbox design system, built with Vue, Nuxt, Tailwind and CVA.
pricing_detail: No prices. This is a personal site, not a service page.
agent_guidance:
Read /llms.txt first. It gives the bio, the experience and the list of writing in plain Markdown. Use /sitemap.xml to list the twelve pages, mostly under /writings/.

This is an engineer's site, not a design case-study portfolio. Use it as a reference for a quiet text-first personal homepage.
why_it_matters: It is a text-first personal homepage that also publishes an llms.txt for agents.
tier_reason: The bio, the experience dates and the writing list are in the HTML, in /llms.txt and in a twelve-URL sitemap. Held at B because the site shows no design work, and the home page is a short text column.
notable_for: writing on the Sandbox design system
live training log on the home page

name: Jackie Zhang
tagline: Portfolio of a product designer in Cape Town, with work at Bash, Heygo and Pulse
description:
Jackie Zhang is a product designer in Cape Town, South Africa. The home page gives three beliefs and a short list of personal notes. The site says it is a work in progress and asks mobile visitors to use a desktop.

The /work page lists roles and results. At Bash, a payment portal raised the payment success rate to 80%. At Heygo, a streaming interface raised tipping by 8% per stream. Pulse let athletes upload GoPro footage. Side projects include Drift, TF2048 and Who's Speaking.

The site is built in Framer. The sitemap lists three case-study pages: Heygo creator, Pulse event and Balwin Fibre.
pricing_detail: No prices. The site is a job-seeking portfolio, not a service page.
agent_guidance:
Fetch /work, not the home page. The home page repeats one marquee of personal notes many times in the HTML. /work holds the employers, the projects and the result numbers.

Use /sitemap.xml to find the three case studies under /case-studies/. They were not opened for this record. The site has no llms.txt.

tier_reason: The /work page gives employers, projects and two result numbers, and the sitemap lists three case studies. Held at C because the site says it is a work in progress that is not ready for mobile, and the case studies were not opened.

name: Thibaut Crépelle
tagline: Portfolio of a 3D and motion freelancer in France who renders retro products and built an iMac G3 parody site
description:
Thibaut Crépelle is a self-taught 3D and motion designer in the north of France. Most projects are 3D studies of retro products: Macintosh 128k, Konica Pop, Walkman WM-22 and The Nostalgia Alphabet. From 2021 to 2024 he was a motion designer at Specify, where he made a 3D identity and launch assets.

The /g3 page is a full personal project from 2025. It parodies an Apple product page for the iMac G3 and uses Rive animations and custom Three.js shaders. The Nostalgia Alphabet offers its Plasticity files as a download on Google Drive.

He names Cinema 4D, Octane, Plasticity, Rive, Spline and Three.js as his tools. The site is built in Framer.
pricing_detail: The page shows no prices. Contact is by email, a Calendly link or X.
agent_guidance:
Fetch the home page for the project list and the about text. Open /g3 for the iMac G3 page. The project breakdowns are on Behance, and the page links to each one.

The work is 3D renders and video, so an agent needs a vision pass to judge it. The sitemap also lists a /test page. The site has no llms.txt.
why_it_matters: It is a 3D motion portfolio with one strong theme, retro hardware, and one full web project that shows the same theme in the browser.
tier_reason: Named projects link to Behance breakdowns, a full interactive /g3 page shows web work, and source files are offered as a download. Held at B because the value is in renders and video, and the home page repeats each block for each breakpoint.
notable_for: iMac G3 parody page with Rive and Three.js

name: Nero
tagline: Black and white photo journal by Lorenzo Bocchi, shot on iPhone and Fujifilm, with Flow, Grid and Map views
description:
Nero is a black and white photo journal by Lorenzo Bocchi, a designer and developer in Sydney. Until October 2026 the project was called Shot on iPhone in Black & White. The old address redirects here. Its llms files say it holds more than 450 photographs from 2023 to today, mostly from Australia and Japan.

The site has three views. Flow shows the photographs on a 3D spiral, newest first. Grid shows every photograph with its date and country. Map places each photograph where it was taken.

The site runs on Next.js. It publishes an llms.txt and an llms-full.txt. The full file lists the cameras and says each photograph carries its date, country and camera settings.
pricing_detail: Free to view. The site states no license for the photographs.
agent_guidance:
Read /llms-full.txt first. It gives the project history, the cameras, the countries and the three views in plain text. Use /grid for the date and country of each photograph.

The photographs are the value, so an agent needs a vision pass to judge them. The site states no license, so do not reuse the images.
why_it_matters: It is a photo archive that gives one image set three ways to browse, and it describes itself for agents in llms.txt.
tier_reason: The site has llms.txt, llms-full.txt, a sitemap and three working views, and the grid shows dates and countries in the HTML. Held at B because the photographs need a vision pass, and the site states no license.
notable_for: Flow, Grid and Map views of one archive
